title: How To Handle A Student Who Doesn't Do Their Work
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents a deliberately counterintuitive strategy for students who refuse to work during independent time: stop approaching them entirely. He argues that the standard instinct — kneeling beside the student, pleading, offering help or rewards — actually makes students more resistant and dependent over time, because motivation has to be generated internally rather than coaxed externally. The concrete technique is to withdraw all one-on-one engagement once independent work begins, letting the discomfort of sitting idle shift full responsibility for the work onto the student rather than the teacher. He pairs this with two supporting commitments: reminding the class collectively (not individually) of the real-world stakes of not learning, and refusing to inflate any grade so students feel the genuine consequences of their choices. The teacher's real job, in his framing, is to deliver a lesson compelling enough that students want to do the work in the first place — not to rescue individual holdouts. He acknowledges the strategy may take repeated attempts before it visibly changes behavior, but claims it eventually works even with students others have labeled unreachable.

The core move is to withdraw all direct one-on-one engagement during independent work, shifting full responsibility onto the student.

quotes: Anything and everything you do directly—as in approaching and engaging with the student—is bound to fail. Because it doesn’t come from within the student.
Motivation and desire to do the work must come from them. It must be their choice and of their volition.
Instead, let them just sit there. That’s right. Once you send your students off to do their independent work, you’re finished speaking or offering additional help.
You will not inflate any grade. You will mark the exact score they earned on their report card, essay, math assignment, reading assessment, etc.
Do this every day. Get really good at it. And you’ll never again have students sitting and doing nothing.
